verified.claim: The badge no longer says 'Not insured' when the chain cannot be read, and that answer is not cacheable
verified.evidence: Production build (NEXT_DIST_DIR=.next-rv) started with next start -p 3108 and RH_TESTNET_RPC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9: /badge/<account> for all 4 covered accounts (0xa93962d5...0C0C, 0x4462A953...d9F4, 0xB792735F...eBEa, 0xdc1F0d95...A0c1) returned HTTP 200 'Bondline: unavailable. chain not readable just now.' with cache-control: no-store (content-type image/svg+xml, access-control-allow-origin *). Repeated on a second build of the current tree at 06:57 IST (2 covered accounts and an EOA: all unavailable, no-store). Further break attempts with a fetch-patching preload in the scratch dir (no second port, nothing in the repo changed): every eth_call failing with JSON-RPC -32000 'execution aborted (timeout = 5s)', -32000 'header not found', HTTP 429, HTTP 500, an HTML 200 body, or -32005 'rate limit exceeded' -> 'unavailable' + no-store (viem retried the HTTP, parse and rate-limit failures: 4 calls each). Failing only the 1st, 2nd or 3rd of the 4 RPC calls a request makes with -32000 -> unavailable + no-store; failing only the 4th (the ProofOfCover read) -> falls back to the cover's health and answers 'Insured' correctly. A single HTTP 500, HTML body or -32005 on any one call was retried and the answer was correct. Design limit, not a regression: an RPC that ANSWERS the first read with '0x' or a code-3 revert is indistinguishable from an EOA and gives 'Not insured' with the public cache header (a lagging replica could do that).

Production build, next start -p 3108, Chromium via Playwright (the letter is rendered in the browser after hydration; the server HTML carries it only in the RSC payload). Results. Account A (live Careful, 2 letters, newest first): both 'Hash matches the text', stored equals computed; one stored hash is upper-case hex and one letter contains é, an emoji, −, · and curly quotes, so the case-insensitive compare and UTF-8 hashing are right. Account B (live Bold), stored text edited after hashing: 'Hash does not match the text', stored 0xa026fa... (cast keccak of the original) versus computed 0x4ba6cf... (cast keccak of the edited text). Account C (replay Bold), stored hash with its last hex digit flipped: 'Hash does not match the text', with the SCRIPTED label. Account D (replay Careful), a dryRun template record: no letter section. The unknown address 0x...dEaD with a letter file: none rendered. Matching: lettersFor() (web/src/lib/letters.ts) keeps a record only if its account equals the page's account case-insensitively, it is not dryRun, and settleTx, account, letter and hash are strings. All four fixture letters carry the same user (the team buyer) and none showed on another account's page (settle txs a1 and a2 only on A, b1 only on B, c1 only on C, nothing on D); a record with no hash, an account value with a leading space, a non-JSON file, a broken JSON file and an array file were all ignored. HTML in a letter or in the model name (an img with onerror, script tags) is shown as plain text, no script ran (no dialog, no injected node) and the hash still matched. No page or console errors. summary: FIRST PASS (superseded by recheckSummary below; kept for the record): Most of E reproduces. The build, lint and types pass; every page loads at 375 and 1440 px with no errors or overflow; the market totals, yields, Careful 13 / Bold 175 bps, gap times, Chainlink restart time and badge states all match my own chain reads and recomputation; Lighthouse mobile is 94 on /live (the builder said 96) and 97 on /party; gated sections (Stylus, proofs, mutation, backtest, letters, ProofOfCover badge) are hidden on the real tree and unlock correctly in a fixture, and the roadmap numbering conflict is fixed. Status is partial because I found one real bug and some overclaims. The badge reports 'Not insured by Bondline' for a covered account when the RPC is down, and the edge caches it for up to a minute. /judge's contract-quality block mixes a source count (142, which I reproduced with forge) that includes the unverified ProofOfCover tests with stale 132-test, coverage and Slither reports that predate ProofOfCover.sol. The /judge line 'every number on this site, read from the chain' is false as worded. Claim letters and the Stylus on-chain call were not verified and remain hidden. The landing page cannot show a paid claim until the 15:00 IST gap settles, and the +34,456% style APY figures, though labelled as short-window, are not meaningful. I sent no transactions, changed nothing outside web/qa/verify-*, and stopped my server on port 3106. I also left my own build folders web/.next-ve, contracts/out-ve and contracts/cache-ve.

fixed.claim: The Insured by Bondline badge never shows a false 'not insured'
fixed.originalProblem: web/src/lib/badge.ts reads cover and market with .catch(() => null) and returns none() when either is null. I restarted the production server with RH_TESTNET_RPC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9 (no chain reachable) and /badge/<covered Bold account> returned HTTP 200 'Not insured by Bondline. no cover on this account.' with Cache-Control public, max-age=30, s-maxage=60. A real RPC outage would put a false 'not insured' on every embedded badge for up to a minute at the edge. The 'unavailable' state only fires when a later read throws.

recheckSummary: Rechecked by an independent re-verifier at the time above (follow-up). Fixed and reproduced: the badge (unchanged since my earlier pass) and the 'Real' wording. New in this pass: the claim letter re-hash check now works on fixture letters (match, mismatch for an edited text and for a wrong hash, dryRun hidden, no cross-account display, no script injection, gate respected), so that entry is out of failed[]; it was a fixture, not a real letter, and the check proves only that the text equals the hash stored beside it. The /judge quality tiles are consistent again because the reports were regenerated at 07:33 IST (170 tests in 13 suites, coverage 701/703 and 125/127, all reproduced by my own forge runs and read on a fresh build), so that entry is out of failed[] too, with the standing caveat that the reports must be regenerated whenever tests change. Status stays partial: two entries cannot be verified yet (the Stylus on-chain call, which is not deployed because activation is paused; and a paid claim, since no Settled event exists). Both remain correctly hidden or honest on the site. Nothing was sent to any chain; deployments/letters stayed absent.
recheckObservations: The re-hash check proves internal consistency only: the hash sits in the same file as the text (a forged file can carry a matching hash), it is not on-chain like a decision hash, and the page does not compare the settle tx or the numbers with the chain.

lettersFor() matches by the record's account field only. It does not check that the settle tx belongs to that account or that the account is Settled, so a letter file named for an Active account would show a 'Claim letter' on its page (the section is rendered whatever the account's status).
The letter section is drawn in the browser after hydration: the server HTML has no letter text (the RSC payload carries it), so with JavaScript off nothing shows. Not a false pass.

The quality tiles are consistent only while contracts/reports/tests.txt, coverage.md and gas.txt are regenerated whenever a .t.sol file is added or removed; workstream A was still adding files when I looked.

Under the Rust (off-chain) rows on /agent the footnote says 'Difference 0.0000 bps (the contract's rounding to 0.0001 bps)': no contract is deployed and the difference is exactly zero. (Workstream B's artefact; reported in B.json's entry.)
